entities.label: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023
entities.desc: The James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 is Public Law 117-263, enacted from H.R. 7776 and approved 23 December 2022 at 136 Stat. 2395. Buried inside a routine defence authorisation of more than a thousand pages is the single most consequential piece of UAP law on this board: it rewrote 50 U.S.C. 3373 to stand up the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office under the Secretary of Defense in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence, within 120 days of enactment. The statute obliges that office to standardise collection and reporting of unidentified anomalous phenomena across the entire Defense and intelligence enterprise, to coordinate with the FAA, NASA and DHS, to run field investigations, to report to Congress in both classified and unclassified form, and - the provision that matters most here - to compile a historical record of US Government involvement with UAP reaching back to 1 January 1945. Congress does not order a seventy-eight-year retrospective historical record of an agency that has nothing to look back on; the 1945 start date is the year of Trinity and of the earliest incidents alleged in the recovery narrative, and it was chosen by legislators who had by then been briefed in closed session. The Act is therefore both the legal instrument that created AARO and, read as an artifact, a congressional acknowledgement that a concealed institutional history exists and needs to be reconstructed. Section 3373 has been amended repeatedly since - by Pub. L. 118-31 and Pub. L. 119-60 - which is the legislative signature of a fight that did not end when the office was created.

claims.text: Enacted as Public Law 117-263 from H.R. 7776, approved 23 December 2022, printed at 136 Stat. 2395 under the short title 'James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023'.

The Act's UAP provisions amended 50 U.S.C. 3373 to require the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the DNI, to establish the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office within 120 days of 23 December 2022.

Statutory duties imposed on the office include standardising UAP collection, reporting and analysis across Defense and the intelligence community; evaluating links to foreign governments or non-state actors; coordinating with FAA, NASA and DHS; conducting field investigations; delivering classified and unclassified reports to Congress; and compiling a historical record of US Government involvement with UAP covering 1 January 1945 onward.

Section 3373 was first enacted by Pub. L. 117-81 (27 Dec 2021) and subsequently amended by Pub. L. 117-263 (23 Dec 2022), Pub. L. 118-31 (22 Dec 2023) and Pub. L. 119-60 (18 Dec 2025) - four successive defence bills reworking the same section.

The 1 January 1945 statutory start date for the historical record is the tell. Congress selected a boundary that predates every public UAP episode and sits at the beginning of the atomic era, which is coherent only if the members writing the provision had been given reason to believe the record they were ordering reconstructed begins there. Reasoning: the date is arbitrary on the 'nothing to find' hypothesis and precise on the recovery hypothesis.

entities.label: Project On Government Oversight
entities.desc: The Project On Government Oversight is a Washington non-profit founded in 1981, originally as a Pentagon procurement watchdog under the name Project on Military Procurement, and later broadened to the whole federal executive. It describes itself as a nonpartisan independent watchdog that investigates, exposes and champions reforms on systemic corruption, abuse of power and waste, and it operates as a donor-funded 501(c)(3) with published audited financials and charity-navigator accreditation rather than on government or contractor money. Its working method is the one that matters to this board: it takes documents and testimony from inside federal agencies and defence contractors, publishes the underlying records, supplies congressional committees with investigative material, and maintains a standing whistleblower intake with legal guidance for people who cannot safely go through their own chain of command. That combination - independence from the contractors, a document-publishing habit and a protected intake channel - makes POGO one of the small number of non-governmental institutions positioned to receive material from inside compartmented programmes and route it to oversight. It sits on the board as infrastructure rather than as a claimant: an external, non-classified path around the internal reporting channels that the concealment depends on.

POGO is donor-funded, publishes audited financials and holds four-star Charity Navigator, CharityWatch and Candid Platinum transparency ratings; it produces investigative reports, policy recommendations and congressional testimony, and maintains published whistleblower resources.

POGO's structural position - contractor-independent funding, a documented whistleblower intake and a direct line into congressional investigative staff - makes it a viable off-ramp for insiders bound by programme non-disclosure agreements who will not use the DoD internal channels. Reasoning: from its documented function, not from any specific UAP disclosure attributed to it here.

entities.label: The Intercept
entities.desc: The Intercept is an investigative news organisation founded in 2014 and built around adversarial reporting on national security, surveillance, civil liberties, criminal justice and technology. It runs as a non-profit funded by reader and listener donations, takes no advertising, and publishes impact reports and audited financial statements; its masthead is led by editor-in-chief Ben Muessig with Annie Chabel as chief executive, under a board that has included Maria Ressa. The outlet was created in the first instance to publish and contextualise leaked classified documents, and it has kept a document-forward house style in which the primary record is posted alongside the story rather than merely characterised. For this board its relevance is the same as POGO's but on the publication side: an institution with secure submission practice, counsel accustomed to classified-information litigation, and no advertiser or defence-contractor dependency, which makes it one of the outlets to which a programme insider can plausibly deliver documents. It is recorded here as part of the disclosure ecosystem's infrastructure, not as a source of UAP claims in itself.

Its founding purpose - publishing leaked classified material with the underlying documents attached - and its advertiser-free funding make it a low-friction destination for compartmented-programme documents. Reasoning: from its stated editorial model and ownership structure.

entities.label: United States Navy
entities.desc: The United States Navy is the maritime service of the Department of Defense, organised under a civilian Secretary of the Navy with the Chief of Naval Operations as senior uniformed officer, and it states its purpose as deploying combat-ready sailors, ships, aircraft and submarines worldwide without dependence on foreign land bases. It is the service that generated the modern evidentiary core of the UAP problem: carrier strike group encounters off southern California in November 2004 and off the eastern seaboard in 2014-2015, recorded by F/A-18 targeting pods, SPY-1 radar and aircrew who filed the reports through operational channels. On 27 April 2020 the Department authorised release of three unclassified Navy videos - one from November 2004 and two from January 2015 - and stated on the record that it was doing so to clear up public misconceptions about whether the circulating footage was real. That release is a hinge artifact for this board, because it converts material that had circulated as leak and rumour into acknowledged official product while conspicuously not addressing what the objects were. The Navy also holds the institutional position that matters for custody questions - it operates the fleet ranges where the encounters occurred, the aviation safety and hazard reporting systems into which aircrew reports flow, and the shore facilities repeatedly named in recovery and material-storage allegations elsewhere on this board.

The Navy is organised under a Secretary of the Navy, Under Secretary, Chief of Naval Operations, Vice Chief and Chief of Naval Personnel, with the stated mission of global deployment to preserve peace, deter aggression and protect American interests without dependence on foreign land bases.

The 2020 release is best read as damage control rather than disclosure: the Department confirmed authenticity, which it could no longer avoid, while declining to characterise the objects, and it released only footage already in public circulation. Reasoning: the release statement's own wording confines the purpose to correcting misconceptions about the existing circulating footage.

entities.label: Enigma Labs
entities.desc: Enigma Labs is a privately held company operating what it calls the world's first platform dedicated to unidentified anomalous phenomena: a mobile and web system that takes sighting reports from the public, pushes real-time proximity alerts, plots an interactive map and exposes a searchable database that it states exceeds 50,000 reports with more than 560,000 alerts sent. It is staffed as a full-time commercial team rather than a volunteer network, and it states editorial neutrality on the origin question - positioning itself as an aggregator of sighting experiences that will 'follow the science wherever it leads'. Its board relevance is custodial: it is one of the few large UAP report corpora held entirely outside government, which means it cannot be classified, reorganised out of existence or narrowed by an agency deciding what counts as a case. The analyst Alejandro Rojas works with Enigma and its dataset has been used to characterise what the government file releases of 2025-2026 do and do not contain. The caveat recorded here is real: the company publishes little about its verification protocol, so the corpus is best treated as an unfiltered intake stream rather than an adjudicated case file.

The company states it remains neutral on the origins of the phenomenon and describes itself as an aggregator of people's sighting experiences.

The published About material describes no verification, validation or de-duplication protocol, so the Enigma corpus should be treated as raw public intake with unknown signal-to-noise, valuable for volume and geography rather than for individual case strength. Reasoning: absence of any stated methodology on the company's own descriptive page.

A privately held report corpus of this size is structurally outside the reach of classification authority, which makes it the natural control set against which government-released datasets can be tested for omissions. Reasoning: from ownership structure, not from any audit performed here.

entities.label: Blue Marble Space Institute of Science
entities.desc: The Blue Marble Space Institute of Science is a Seattle-based non-profit public charity organised under section 501(c)(3), describing itself as an international community engaged in building a sustainable future and nurturing public scientific interest. Its research is interdisciplinary and centred on planetary habitability, the origin of life, space biology, climate, sustainable development, human spaceflight and solar system exploration, published in peer-reviewed journals and pushed outward through seminars, podcasts and its SAGANet network; every project it takes on is required to include an educational outreach component. It is not a UAP institute, and that is precisely why it matters here: it is the institutional home of the astrobiologist Jacob Haqq-Misra, whose work on technosignatures and on the methodology of anomaly search brought conventional astrobiology standards into direct contact with the UAP question, and who sits on the Sol Foundation advisory board and was named in June 2026 to the UAP Science Advisory Council. BMSIS therefore functions on this board as one of the bridges by which the phenomenon is being carried out of the classified world and into ordinary peer-reviewed science - a route that does not require any agency's permission and cannot be shut by reclassification.

BMSIS's board significance is derivative rather than programmatic: it supplies an academically legitimate, government-independent affiliation for Jacob Haqq-Misra, allowing UAP-adjacent anomaly-search methodology to be published under an astrobiology institute's name. Reasoning: from the institute's stated remit combined with Haqq-Misra's recorded affiliation elsewhere on this board.

entities.label: Office of the Chief Science Advisor of Canada
entities.desc: The Office of the Chief Science Advisor of Canada (OCSA) is the federal science-advice body that reports into the Government of Canada's science portfolio and advises the Prime Minister and the Minister of Innovation, Science and Industry. In 2022-2025 it ran the Sky Canada Project, a formal review of how public reports of unidentified aerial phenomena are handled in Canada, and on 30 June 2025 it published 'Management of Public Reporting of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in Canada', a 59-page report of the project. The report is careful about its own limits - it explicitly states it is not intended to collect first-hand data, not to make OCSA the reporting point of contact, and not to prove or disprove extraterrestrial life or visitation - but it does something more useful for this board: it maps the actual Canadian reporting landscape, naming Transport Canada's CADORS occurrence system, the RCAF and Department of National Defence, the National Research Council's 1967-1990s collection role, and the RCMP, OPP and Sûreté du Québec as de facto intake points, and it finds the whole arrangement fragmented and gap-ridden. Its recommendations - identify the department that owns public UAP data, stand up a dedicated service that investigates and publishes its analyses, and have Transport Canada and NAV CANADA actively encourage aircrew and controllers to report without stigma - amount to a Western government stating on the record that stigma suppresses reporting and that transparency is the corrective. OCSA sits on this board as the clearest case of a G7 science authority treating UAP as a legitimate data-governance problem rather than as a subject to be denied.

A national science advisor publishing a finding that aircrew do not report because of stigma is an official admission that the observational record is systematically incomplete by social mechanism - which is the same mechanism a concealment programme would rely on and would not need to enforce. Reasoning: stated in the report's own recommendation to remove fear of stigmatisation.

entities.label: Canada Department of Transport
entities.desc: The Department of Transport - today Transport Canada - is the federal department responsible for civil aviation regulation and transportation safety in Canada, and it holds two distinct positions in this record. In 1950 it granted one of its own engineers, Wilbert B. Smith, permission to conduct part-time research into whether some UFOs might use the Earth's magnetic field as a propulsion source; the work became Project Magnet, Smith expanded it to include assessment of the validity of UFO observations, he launched a balloon over Ottawa to monitor public and media reaction, and he established a UFO observatory outside the capital. This makes the Canadian Department of Transport one of the earliest documented instances of a Western government funding a UAP propulsion-physics inquiry inside a civil - not military - department, and Smith's own contemporaneous memoranda are the reason the Canadian file is cited so often against official denial. The second position is current: Transport Canada operates the Civil Aviation Daily Occurrence Reporting System (CADORS), which logs occurrences affecting aviation safety including UAP sightings, making it the principal live federal intake for Canadian aircrew reports. Canada's own Chief Science Advisor named Transport Canada in its June 2025 Sky Canada report as the body that should, with NAV CANADA, actively encourage pilots and controllers to report sightings without stigma - an acknowledgement by one arm of government that the aviation reporting channel it already owns is being under-used.

entities.label: DGAC Chile — Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil
entities.desc: The Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil is Chile's civil aviation authority, and it is the only such body in the hemisphere to have operated a permanent, publicly acknowledged office for the study of anomalous aerial phenomena for nearly three decades. On 3 October 1997 the DGAC created the Comité de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (CEFAA); on 18 October 2021 it reorganised that committee by Resolución Exenta N° 04/3/0113/1385 into the Sección de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (SEFAA), placing it under the DGAC's Communications Subdepartment. SEFAA takes case submissions from the public through an official reporting channel, analyses them by declared scientific method with emphasis on audiovisual evidence, and publishes a case database organised by year - the analyses go out, not just the intake. Under General Ricardo Bermúdez, who directed CEFAA from 1997 to 2016, the office released military sensor footage and published its own conclusions on cases it could not resolve. Chile matters to this board as a control case: a state with real air-defence equities ran an open UAP office for twenty-nine years and released classified-origin footage without the consequences the American concealment argument depends on, and Canada's Chief Science Advisor identified it in June 2025 as one of only three national models worth copying alongside AARO and France's GEIPAN.

SEFAA investigates reports using declared scientific method with emphasis on audiovisual evidence, accepts public case submissions through an official reporting system, and maintains a public database of resolved cases organised by year.

Chile's twenty-nine-year run of an open civil-aviation UAP office, publishing analyses and releasing military-origin footage, shifts the burden of proof onto the party claiming that public handling of UAP data would cause unacceptable harm. Reasoning: the predicted harms did not materialise in a state with comparable air-sovereignty concerns.

entities.label: 509th Bomb Group
entities.desc: The 509th was constituted as the 509th Composite Group in December 1944 as the delivery unit for the atomic bomb, flew the August 1945 atomic missions, and was redesignated the 509th Bomb Group and based at Roswell Army Air Field in New Mexico - in 1947 the only atomic-capable combat unit in the world. That is the most important fact about the Roswell episode and the one most often dropped from it: the press release announcing that the 509th had recovered a 'flying disc' came from the public information office of the unit holding the nuclear mission, staffed by officers with the highest clearances then in existence, and it was retracted within hours. The GAO's 1995 audit found the group's own July 1947 unit history recording that the RAAF public information office 'was kept quite busy ... answering inquiries on the flying disc' and stating that the object 'turned out to be a radar tracking balloon'. The same audit produced the finding that anchors this node: the RAAF administrative records for March 1945 to December 1949 and its outgoing messages for October 1946 to December 1949 were destroyed, and the disposition form does not indicate what organisation or person destroyed them, when, or under what authority. A base's entire administrative and message traffic for the period bracketing the incident is gone, with no accountable destruction authority recorded, at the one installation where records discipline was most rigorous. The 509th is therefore not merely the unit at the centre of the founding incident; it is the point at which the documentary record was removed.

Unaccounted destruction of four years of administrative files and message traffic at the base hosting the world's only atomic-capable combat unit is not ordinary records management. Reasoning: routine disposition under schedule leaves an accountable authority and a date on the disposition form, and GAO found neither.

entities.label: SAF/AAZ — Air Force Declassification & Special Programs
entities.desc: SAF/AAZ is the Secretary of the Air Force's Director of Security, Counterintelligence and Special Program Oversight, an office of the Air Force Secretariat sitting under the Administrative Assistant to the Secretary (SAF/AA). Air Force Instruction 16-701, 'Management, Administration and Oversight of Special Access Programs' (18 February 2014, OPR SAF/AAZE, certified by SAF/AAZ), assigns it the controlling role over every Air Force special access programme: SAF/AAZ is principal advisor to SAF/AA for SAPs, serves as Director of the Air Force SAP Central Office (AF SAPCO), develops SAP policy, directs and oversees the SAP security programme, serves as Designated Accreditation Authority for all SAP information systems, and serves as the access approval authority for all SAPs with power to approve waivers for SAP access. The same instruction directs SAF/AAZ to 'establish a declassification program' and to ensure information is neither classified longer than necessary nor declassified prematurely - meaning that the office that grants access to Air Force black programmes is also the office that decides when their contents may be released. That concentration is why this node matters. Any Air Force-hosted programme of the kind alleged on this board would be waived or unacknowledged under SAF/AAZ's oversight, its read-on list would be approved there, and any declassification would have to pass the same desk; it is simultaneously the gatekeeper of the secret and the arbiter of its disclosure, which is the structural conflict at the centre of the whole concealment argument.

Para. 2.1 assigns the Director, Security and Special Program Oversight (SAF/AAZ) to serve as principal advisor to SAF/AA for SAPs and as Director, AF SAPCO, developing SAP policy and directing, administering and overseeing the SAP security programme.

Para. 2.1.2.4 directs SAF/AAZ to 'establish a declassification program and ensure that necessary resources are applied to the review of information to ensure it is neither classified for longer than necessary nor declassified prematurely in accordance with the file series exemption'.

SAF/AAZ serves as Designated Accreditation Authority for all SAP information systems and as access approval authority for all SAPs, approving waivers for SAP access; both authorities may be delegated only in writing and must be revalidated annually.
The 2014 edition of AFI 16-701 was certified by SAF/AAZ, then Mr. Daniel F. McMillin, with SAF/AAZE as office of primary responsibility.

Placing SAP access approval and SAP declassification authority in the same office means the decision to disclose a programme is made by the official whose institutional interest is in the programme's continued protection. Reasoning: directly from the two responsibilities assigned in AFI 16-701 paras. 2.1.2.4 and 2.1.2.7.

entities.label: Wayne State University
entities.desc: Wayne State University is a public research university in Midtown Detroit, founded in 1868 when five physicians established the Detroit Medical College, and now comprising thirteen schools and colleges - the School of Medicine among them - with over 24,000 students and a self-described position as Michigan's premier urban research institution. Its place on this board is not institutional but personal: Wayne State's School of Medicine is where Christopher 'Kit' Green did his academic work after leaving the CIA, where he had run life-sciences analysis in the Office of Scientific Intelligence and monitored the SRI parapsychology programme. Green wrote the AAWSAP Defense Intelligence Reference Document on anomalous acute and subacute field effects on human biological tissues, and he examined and documented injuries reported by people claiming close-proximity encounters. That single affiliation makes Wayne State the civilian academic address for the medical-effects strand of the programme record - the strand that treats the phenomenon as something that leaves clinical evidence in human beings rather than only radar returns. The university itself has no documented programme role and is recorded here as the institutional locus of that work.

entities.label: Vanderbilt University
entities.desc: Vanderbilt University and Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee are on this board because of a single line of published work: Stephen Bruehl, professor in the Department of Anesthesiology at VUMC, is the lead author of the October 2025 Scientific Reports paper 'Transients in the Palomar Observatory Sky Survey (POSS-I) may be associated with nuclear testing and reports of unidentified anomalous phenomena', written with Beatriz Villarroel of Nordita. The paper reports that star-like transients on photographic plates from 1949-1957 were about 45 per cent more likely on dates within a day of nuclear testing, and that each additional UAP report on a given date corresponded to an 8.5 per cent increase in transient observations. Bruehl also authored the SCU cluster analysis of features in 216 selected UAP reports. What matters here is the venue and the affiliation, not only the result: a Nature Portfolio journal accepted a statistical association between nuclear testing, UAP reports and an archival astronomical dataset, submitted under a major American medical school's name. That is the phenomenon entering the ordinary peer-reviewed literature by a route no classification authority controls, and Vanderbilt is the institution whose name is on it.

Publication of this analysis in a Nature Portfolio journal under a Vanderbilt medical affiliation marks a change in what the mainstream literature will accept, and it is the kind of result that cannot be retracted by an agency decision. Reasoning: from the venue and the institutional affiliation on the paper.

entities.label: Sheffield Hallam University
entities.desc: Sheffield Hallam University is a large applied university in Sheffield, England, with a City Campus on Howard Street, roughly 31,000 students and 4,000 staff, and a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework. It matters to this board as the academic base of Dr David Clarke, the journalism academic who did more than anyone to prise open the British official record: the Freedom of Information campaign that forced release of the Ministry of Defence's Project Condign study, and the consultancy to The National Archives on the MoD UFO files release programme of 2008-2013. Clarke's outputs are deposited in the university's own institutional repository, SHURA, which holds his National Archives UFO-files media and podcast records from that project, his books on the UFO files and on the history of the phenomenon as a modern myth, and his co-authored report on aerial phenomena observed near the Channel Islands in April 2007. The same repository also holds Andrew Robinson's 2025 photographic analysis of the Calvine photograph, the best-known unresolved British UAP image. Sheffield Hallam therefore functions as an archival and evidentiary node rather than a research programme: it is the university whose repository preserves the working record of the person who forced the British files open, which is exactly the sort of independently held documentation a concealment cannot quietly reabsorb.

entities.label: IZMIRAN — Pushkov Institute of Terrestrial Magnetism
entities.desc: IZMIRAN is the N.V. Pushkov Institute of Terrestrial Magnetism, Ionosphere and Radio Wave Propagation of the Russian Academy of Sciences, founded in 1939 and based at Troitsk outside Moscow, with a branch in St Petersburg. Its published work covers geomagnetism, the ionosphere, solar-terrestrial physics, space weather forecasting and radio propagation - the exact disciplines a state would draw on to explain, or to investigate, unexplained atmospheric optical and radar phenomena. That is why it appears on this board: IZMIRAN is the institutional home of the physicist Yury Platov, identified in the secondary literature as chief executive of SETKA-AN, the USSR Academy of Sciences half of the 1978-1990 Soviet state programme on anomalous phenomena that ran alongside the Ministry of Defence's SETKA-MO, and as co-author of the official history of that programme. The Soviet arrangement is instructive by contrast with the American one: the academy side of the programme sat in a named, publicly listed research institute that still exists and still publishes, rather than inside an unacknowledged compartment, which is why the Russian programme has an attributable institutional address at all. No primary Russian archival document establishing IZMIRAN's SETKA role was obtained in this pass, and that is recorded as a gap.

entities.label: Senado Federal do Brasil
entities.desc: The Senado Federal is the upper chamber of Brazil's National Congress, composed of 81 senators - three for each of the 26 states and the Federal District - elected to eight-year terms, with the constitutional powers of legislative revision, treaty approval, confirmation of senior appointments and the summoning of ministers and officials to give evidence. Its relevance to this board is carried by Senator Eduardo Girão of Ceará (Senate member code 5976, elected for the 56th legislature and continuing into the 57th), who has pressed publicly for the Brazilian state's UAP record to be opened and who brought the January 1996 Varginha case to Capitol Hill on its thirtieth anniversary in 2026. Brazil is a comparative test case for the concealment thesis in a way few countries are: its military UFO files were transferred to the Arquivo Nacional and made citizen-accessible, and the 1986 air force incident is documented in that archive, so Brazil has already done what the American programme is alleged to be preventing. A national legislature that can summon officials, and that contains a member actively pursuing the Varginha file, is a live route by which the non-US half of the record can be forced open - and it is a route the United States cannot classify. No primary Senate legislative instrument on UAP was located in this pass; the Senate's keyword search service for legislative matters has been deprecated and its replacement returns unfiltered results.

entities.label: Hospital Regional de Varginha
entities.desc: The facility referred to in the Varginha literature as the Hospital Regional de Varginha is registered in Brazil's national health-establishment register, CNES, as the Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas, CNES code 2761041, at Rua Rui Barbosa 158, Centro, Varginha, Minas Gerais (CEP 37002-140), under municipal administration, operating continuous 24-hour service and providing SUS outpatient care. Varginha's other registered hospitals in the same register include the Hospital Bom Pastor, run by the municipal hospital foundation, and the Hospital Unimed Varginha. The hospital is on this board because it is one of the medical facilities named in the January 1996 Varginha case as a place to which an injured creature was reportedly taken and held before being moved on, in the sequence involving military and fire-brigade personnel that is recorded elsewhere on this board as ev-varginha-1996. The case is not a historical curiosity: it was carried to Capitol Hill on its thirtieth anniversary, and on 8 July 2026 a congressional demand went to the CIA and FBI for records on the Varginha and Campinas incidents - meaning that a municipal hospital in Minas Gerais is now a named location in an American records fight. What exists here as verified fact is the facility and its registry entry; the 1996 hospital-custody sequence rests on witness testimony and journalism, not on any hospital record obtained in this pass.
